title: Fragmentary Greek funerary inscription
support: A rectangular cippus/stele of the local limestone, finished smooth on all sides. Intact left and part of front and base and lower right, but damaged across the upper right. The top is preserved at the upper left, but the top of the face is lost, and theoretically there is space for a first line of text, if it were inscribed right up to the top of the front face (unlikely).

layout.p: Two visible lines of Greek letters, decreasing in size, across the upper part of the front face. Line 1 more widely spaced than line 2 and slightly inset.

handNote.lettering: Elegant thinly carved letters. The trace of sigma on line 1 suggests a rather open four-bar sigma; Epsilon has short middle bar; Pi has short right hand hasta; omicron is sligthly smaller than other letters; Mu has vertical outer strokes, half-length inner strokes.

date._: fourth century BCE on palaeographic grounds

provenanceFound._: Acquired by Orsi, 2 November 1905 (so the inventory), from Predio Tarantello, a continuation of the Tor di Conte early Hellenistic necropolis ; now in storage in the archaeological park of Neapolis

museum.name: Museo Archeologico Regionale Paolo Orsi
museum.description: An outstanding collection of archaeological material. The collection ranges from Siracusa and the surrounding territory (Megara Hyblaia, Akrai, Kasmenai etc) to encompass all of eastern Sicily, reaching as far as Gela and Agrigento. The ground floor covers prehistory through to the end of the Classical period. Upstairs includes Hellenistic and Roman Syracuse and a display of material from the catacombs. A gallery displaying material from Hellenistic eastern Sicily is in preparation.
